title: かける and かかる: the all-purpose pair
summary: A long list of meanings becomes one picture: hang something so that it stays. かける is the other-move verb, かかる the self-move verb.

blocks.text: Dictionaries give かける twenty or more meanings. They all come from one picture: **hang or hook** something on something, so that it **clings** and does not easily fall off. It is neither "put" nor "hang" in English, and **かける** (other-move) and **かかる** (self-move) are a pair.
Each row below is one picture of hanging or hooking something on something. The picture is the method: if you can see the thing clinging, you know the verb.

rows: a blanket drapes over the sides
ごはんにふりかけをかける
trouble is put on someone and stays
the old bar hung across a door
your hips hang on the seat

blocks.text: The last two are old pictures: a heavy bar hung across a door was the lock and the key at once, and sitting means hanging your hips on the seat.
Two more are common in everyday talk: making a call, and the call that comes in. A call is hung on the other person, and for them it hangs on to them.

blocks.jp: さくらから電話がかかった。
blocks.en: A call came in from Sakura. (the self-move partner)

blocks.jp: 先生に迷惑をかけてしまった。
blocks.en: I have caused the teacher trouble.

blocks.text: **時間がかかる** is not "it takes time" but "time hangs" (on the activity). With the other-move verb you spend it on purpose: **時間をかける**. This is the same pair as lesson 15: が with the self-move verb, を with the other-move verb.

blocks.jp: 日本語を覚えるのに時間がかかる。
この仕事にはお金がかかる。

blocks.text: 時間をかける: you spend the time on purpose.
時間がかかる: the time hangs on by itself.
かける on the い-stem

After the い-stem of a verb, **かける** hooks the action onto something. 話しかける hooks a conversation onto someone: you start speaking to them. 食べかける means you have started eating but not finished, which is why 食べかけ is "half-eaten".

blocks.jp: 駅で友達に話しかけた。
blocks.en: I spoke to my friend at the station.

blocks.jp: 食べかけのパンを机に置いた。
blocks.en: I put the half-eaten bread on the desk.

blocks.jp: これは読みかけの本です。
blocks.en: This is a book I have half read.

items: **かける**: hang or hook something on (cover, wear, call, lock, spend).
**かかる**: it hangs on: time and money "hang" on a task; a call comes in.
After an い-stem, かける hooks the action on: 話しかける, 食べかけ.
The core feeling: stuck on, not easily dislodged.

questions.prompt: この旅行には三万円＿＿かかる。
questions.en: This trip costs thirty thousand yen.
questions.note: かかる is self-move: the money is the carriage.

questions.prompt: 毎日、日本語の勉強に時間＿＿かける。
questions.en: (I) spend time on studying Japanese every day.
questions.note: かける is other-move: you spend time on purpose, so を.
You make a phone call: other-move かける.

questions.prompt: 家から駅まで歩くと、二十分＿＿。
questions.en: Walking from home to the station takes twenty minutes.
questions.note: Time hangs on the walk: self-move かかる.

questions.instruction: Which sentence means "I spent a lot of time on this report"?
options: このレポートに時間がかかった。
このレポートに時間をかけた。
このレポートの時間をかけた。
このレポートが時間をかけた。
questions.note: On purpose, so other-move かける with を.

questions.instruction: What does かける picture here?
questions.prompt: 人に迷惑をかけないでください。
questions.en: Please don't cause trouble for people.
questions.note: 迷惑をかける = put annoyance on someone.

questions.instruction: Tap the part that hangs on the seat
questions.en: (I) sat down on the bench in the park and rested.
questions.note: 腰をかける: you hang your hips on the seat.

questions.en: This dish takes time to make.
questions.note: The time hangs on the cooking by itself: かかる.

questions.en: (I) spent time on my child's studies.
questions.note: かけた takes を: you put time on it.
電話をかける: make a phone call.
お金が + かかる: money hangs on it.

questions.prompt: At night, (I) lock the door, too.
questions.en: At night, (I) lock the door, too.
questions.note: 鍵をかける: lock.

questions.prompt: From home to the station it takes ten minutes.
questions.en: From home to the station it takes ten minutes.
questions.note: Time hangs on the trip: かかる.

questions.instruction: What is the core picture of かける?
options: Hang or hook something on so it clings
questions.note: Neither "put" nor "hang" exactly: it stays stuck on.

questions.instruction: True or false? かかる is the self-move partner of かける.
questions.note: かける / かかる are a pair.

questions.instruction: Which one means to spend time on purpose?
questions.note: The other-move verb with を.
Self-move かかる takes が.
かかる is self-move and cannot take を.

questions.instruction: What does かけた picture here?
options: Putting your voice onto someone, i.e. calling out
questions.note: The voice "hangs" on the other person.
かかる hangs by itself; かける hangs it on.

questions.instruction: True or false? 時間をかける means "it takes time".
questions.note: That is 時間がかかる; with を you spend it on purpose.

questions.prompt: 寒いので、子供にふとんを＿＿＿。
questions.en: Since it was cold, (I) put a futon over the child.
questions.note: You put it over the child: other-move かける, past.

questions.instruction: What does かけ add to a verb's い-stem?
questions.prompt: 食べかけのパンがある。
questions.note: Verb stem + かけ: the action is hooked on, not done.

questions.instruction: Which sentence means "I spoke to a stranger"?
options: 知らない人に話しかけた。
知らない人を話しかかった。
知らない人が話しかけた。
知らない人で話しかかった。
questions.note: Stem + かける: hook a conversation on someone (に).
